name: Sierra Leone
summary: A peninsula where rainforest mountains come down to white sand, Tiwai island with eleven primate species, and the Banana and Turtle Islands offshore — the best beaches in West Africa with almost nobody on them.
when: November to April. The rains here are among the heaviest in Africa.

entries.caption: The Freetown Peninsula
entries.description: Forested mountains dropping straight into the Atlantic, with beaches in every bay.
entries.subject: forested hills coming down to white sand at River No. 2 beach

entries.caption: The Loma Mountains
entries.description: Cloud forest and montane grassland in the northeast, hardly walked at all.
entries.subject: montane grassland and forest in the Loma mountains

entries.caption: Eleven Primates at Tiwai
entries.description: An island in the Moa river with one of the highest primate densities anywhere.
entries.subject: a Diana monkey in the canopy on Tiwai island

entries.caption: Forest, Not Plain
entries.description: Pygmy hippo, forest elephant and bongo in Gola — a forest circuit, not a savanna one.
entries.subject: dense Gola rainforest canopy from a ridge

entries.caption: Bintumani
entries.description: 1,945 metres in the Loma range, the highest point in West Africa west of Cameroon.
entries.subject: the grassy summit ridge of Mount Bintumani above cloud

entries.caption: Charlotte and Bumbuna
entries.description: Charlotte falls in the peninsula forest, and Bumbuna on the Rokel in the interior.
entries.subject: the Charlotte waterfall falling through forest near Freetown

entries.caption: The Moa and the Rokel
entries.description: The Moa runs past Tiwai, and the Rokel comes down to the estuary at Freetown.
entries.subject: the wide Moa river running past forested banks at Tiwai

entries.caption: River No. 2 and the Banana Islands
entries.description: White sand, forest behind, and two small islands an hour offshore with reef around them.
entries.subject: the white sand and green forest of River No. 2 beach

entries.caption: Gola Rainforest
entries.description: The largest remaining block of Upper Guinean forest, now a transboundary park with Liberia.
entries.subject: the closed canopy of Gola rainforest from above

entries.caption: Surfing and Forest Walking
entries.description: Bureh has a surf club run by the village, and Tiwai has night walks for pottos.
entries.subject: surfers waiting for a set at Bureh beach

entries.caption: Krio, and Sixteen Others
entries.description: Freetown was founded by freed slaves, and Krio is the language and the culture that came of it.
entries.subject: a Krio board house with fretwork balconies in Freetown

entries.caption: Mende, Temne and Krio
entries.description: Mende in the south, Temne in the north, and the Krio of the peninsula.
entries.subject: a Mende village gathering under a large tree

entries.caption: Cassava Leaf and Country Rice
entries.description: Cassava leaf with palm oil, groundnut stew, and fish straight off the beach.
entries.subject: a bowl of cassava leaf stew with rice

entries.caption: Lantern Parade
entries.description: Illuminated floats through Freetown on the night of Independence Day.
entries.subject: illuminated lantern floats moving through Freetown at night

entries.caption: Country Cloth and Gara
entries.description: Hand-woven country cloth strips, and gara tie-dye in indigo and kola.
entries.subject: gara tie-dyed cloth drying in a Freetown yard

entries.caption: Bunce Island
entries.description: A slaving fort in the estuary, ruined and overgrown, and among the most affecting in Africa.
entries.subject: the ruined stone walls of Bunce Island fort among trees

entries.caption: The Cotton Tree, and What Followed
entries.description: Freetown grew around one tree where freed slaves gave thanks in 1792.
entries.subject: the historic Cotton Tree standing in central Freetown

entries.caption: Freetown
entries.description: Krio board houses on the hills, the estuary below, and mountains directly behind.
entries.subject: Freetown's hills and harbour seen from above

entries.caption: Krio Board Houses
entries.description: Timber-framed, shuttered, verandahed — an architecture that came back across the Atlantic.
entries.subject: a two-storey Krio board house with shutters and a verandah

entries.caption: Sunday at Lumley
entries.description: The whole city goes to the beach, and the bars along it play until late.
entries.subject: crowds and beach bars at Lumley beach on a Sunday

entries.caption: Beaches With Shade
entries.description: River No. 2 and Tokeh have forest behind the sand and calm water in the dry season.
entries.subject: a family under trees at the edge of River No. 2 beach

entries.caption: Climbing Bintumani
entries.description: Four days from Sinekoro, through forest and out onto grassland above the cloud.
entries.subject: a walker crossing montane grassland on Bintumani

entries.caption: Growing
entries.description: Good beach lodges on the peninsula, and Tiwai's community camp inland.
entries.subject: a beach lodge among palms at Tokeh

entries.caption: Tiwai, Community-Run
entries.description: Eight villages own the island reserve and have done since before the war.
entries.subject: a community guide leading a walk on Tiwai island

entries.caption: Forest Meeting Sand
entries.description: The peninsula beaches in the late afternoon, when the hills behind them go blue.
entries.subject: forested hills behind a beach in late afternoon light

entries.caption: The Turtle Islands
entries.description: Eight sand islands in the far south, reachable only by boat, with no electricity.
entries.subject: a sandbar island with palms and a fishing village in the Turtle Islands

entries.caption: Why Sierra Leone
entries.description: The best beaches in West Africa, with rainforest mountains standing behind them.
entries.subject: an empty white beach below forested hills at dusk
